message_en: Hello and welcome! Please, select your language:
Using this app, you can: 1- Customise your own 3D model, 2- Prepare and visualise the instructions for your 3D Printer (G-Code file), 3- Export the G-Code file and 3D model for 3D Printing.
First, click the (1) DESIGN button in the top bar and adjust parameters in the Shape, Texture, and Deformations boxes.
Next, once satisfied with your design, click (2) CALCULATE to generate G-Code file.
The G-CODE file contains all the instructions the 3D printer needs to follow to print your model.
You can visualise these instructions as an animation by pressing the Play button of the the G-Code player.
Finally, Click (3) SAVE in the top bar, and select "SAVE G-CODE" to export your file.
Navigation: You can zoom, and rotate the 3D model using your fingers (touchscreen) or mouse (Left and Middle buttons).
Need more help? Drag and drop me onto any area of the screen, and I will provide information about the selected section.
You can customise the 3D model by changing the parameters in the Shape, Texture, and Deformations boxes below.
Drop me onto the boxes below for more information.
By modifying the "SHAPE" parameters, you can change the 3D model shape and adjust the number of sides.
The base diametre and height of your model can be adjusted here.
By modifying the "TEXTURE" parameters, you can add different textures to the 3D model.
By modifying the "DEFORMATIONS" parameters, you can apply different deformations to the 3D model.
"APPEARANCE" allows you to change the colour of the 3D model on the screen.
The colour on the screen will not be the colour of your 3D printed model.
The colour of your 3D printed model will be the same as the colour of the paste used for printing it.
To 3D print your model, the printer needs instructions specifying where to deposit material, at what speed, and in what quantity.
These instructions are stored in a G-Code file, where each line contains a separate command for the printer.
You can use the interface below to visualise the G-Code instructions.
Drag and drop me onto the boxes below for more information.
Use the "G-CODE PLAYER" buttons to play the G-Code instructions, either one by one or layer by layer.
You can adjust the animation speed, or change the display from 2D (PATH) to 3D (3D MODEL).
The "PLAYBACK PROGRESS" bars display information such as:
Which line of the G-Code file is currently being displayed,
The estimated build time,
The height level at which the material is being deposited.
The "G-CODE COMMAND" shows the the G-Code instruction displayed on the screen.
The "G-CODE COMMAND DESCRIPTION" describes inplain text form the G-Code instruction displayed on the screen.
In the boxes below you can name your file and export it in various formats.
Drop me onto the boxes below for more information.
Give a name to your model here.
Save the G-Code instructions for 3D printing your model by clicking "SAVE G-CODE"
You can save your model to retrieve later into this App by clicking "SAVE AS .CUP FILE"
You can save your model as a 3D shape in STL format.
STL is a standardised format recognised by all 3D printers and most 3D modeling applications.
Before saving your model as an STL file you must:
1- Specify/adjust the wall thickness for your model
2- Click the "STL PREVIEW" button to visualise the STL file (Optional).
The resolution of the STL file can be changed using the "STL QUALITY" slider.
Higher resolution files will produce smoother surfaces but result in larger STL files (more memory usage)
3- Click the "SAVE AS A SOLID MODEL" button.
Note: Saving your model as a surface models will result in a model with no thickness that cannot be 3D printed.
You can take a picture (.JPG) of your 3D model to share with your friends or print on paper by clicking "SAVE PICTURE"
You can change the 3D Printer and Model Default settings in this menu.
Make sure to click the “Apply Settings” button to apply and activate your changes.
Note: All setting changes are temporary and will reset to the default settings when the app restarts.
To keep your custom settings, you can export them and re-import them in your next session.
Drop me onto the boxes below for more information.
The "3D PRINTER SETTINGS" are parameters that are used to generate the G-Code file.
You can adjust the default settings to improve the quality of your 3D Prints.
Make sure to click the “Apply Settings” button to apply and activate your changes.
Note: All setting changes are temporary and will reset to the default settings when the app restarts.
To keep your custom settings, you can export them and re-import them in your next session.
Unlocking the "MODEL SETTINGS" will provide additional capabilities when designing your 3D model.
Use Import Model to load previously created models.
Toggle App language between Welsh and English.
Turn me ON/OFF depending on whether you want assistance.
Drag and drop me onto any area of the screen, and I will provide information about the selected section.
Use the view presets to quickly rotate the model to standard views such as Top, Front, Side, or Default 3D.
Show or hide a 10 mm grid on the baseplate.
Show or Hide the 3D printer baseplate.
Show or hide the coordinate system used by the 3D printer to determine position in space.
Show or hide the build volume, which represents the printer’s maximum printable area.
This window displays the dimensions (in millimeters), and volume (in cubic centimeters) of your model.
To customise your 3D model, adjust the Shape, Texture, and Deformations settings in the Design Parameters Menu on the left.
This is the path represent the trajectory the 3D printer needs to follow to print your 3D model.
It is made up of a succession of small straight movements.
The instructions for each of these moves are stored as individual text lines within the G-code file.
Each line of the G-Code file tells the printer: Where to move, how fast to go, and  how much material to deposit.
You can use the menu on the left to see and preview how the printer will follow these instructions.
